question.text: Under SEBI AIF Regulations, what is the MINIMUM investment that a NON-employee, NON-accredited investor must commit to a Cat II AIF scheme?

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Regulation 10(c) of SEBI (AIF) Regulations 2012 mandates a minimum investment of INR 1 crore per investor per scheme for ordinary investors. Employees / directors of the manager and Accredited Investors can invest a lower minimum of INR 25 lakh. **The Trap:** INR 25 lakh is the concessional floor for employees/AIs. INR 50 lakh doesn't exist. INR 5 crore is the sponsor minimum commitment benchmark, not the ordinary LP floor. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-A and XIX-C both test INR 1 crore. XXI-B (PMS) tests INR 50 lakh minimum - do NOT confuse. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** At a first close, reject subscriptions below INR 1 crore unless the investor qualifies as an AI (certified by an Accreditation Agency) or is an employee - otherwise SEBI will flag the scheme.
